newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania privatisation fund denies irregularities.
newsitem.headline: Romania privatisation fund denies irregularities.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency rejected as groundless a financial control body report alleging irregularities in its evaluation of company assets.
"The State Ownership Fund (FPS) sells shares, not assets such as land or buildings," said Dan Gabriel Mihut, head of the FPS's budget department, at a news conference on Tuesday.
His remarks were in response to a Court of Accounts report pointing to undervaluation of assets and capital of 363 firms.
The FPS -- created late in 1992 as the holder of 70 percent of around 6,500 companies -- has sold shares in some 3,000 firms so far at prices set by the play of demand and offer, Mihut said.
Evaluation and control of company assets are tasks for managers, auditors and Finance Ministry and Court of Accounts control bodies and not of the FPS as shareholder, he added.
Over the past few days, similar attacks came from local media and Economic Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu.
Spineanu told a local newspaper on Monday the FPS had sold shares of around 600 companies at undervalued prices.

"I have made a study which shows the average price of the shares the FPS sold over the past four years to be 1.3 times higher than the nominal value," National Economy Institute manager Gheorghe Zaman said during the same news conference.
The Court of Accounts report coincided with a shakeup of the FPS's administration board.

Over the past week, the government, the lower house of parliament and the presidency revoked some of the 17 board members, replacing them with members of the coalition which has ruled Romania since general elections last November.
The move, to be followed soon by similar replacements from the upper house of parliament, was dubbed "political cleansing" by the former ruling Party of Social Democracy.
"The rules say board members can be revoked for serious offences. These serious offences should have been demonstrated before the replacements," FPS president Emil Dima said.
The FPS, which has handled most privatisations in Romania so far, has been accused of stalling the selloff process.
"The new government has pledged to step up selloffs, which it cannot do as long as the main privatisation body is managed by people of the old guard," a local economist said.
